Five personas reach Foundry agents and MCP tools through one gateway; the data plane has the last word
Agents Behind the Wall - diagram 01 of 13 - generated by docs/diagrams/build_diagrams.py
- Four walls in order: Foundry guardrail (W0, detective), APIM gateway (W1), MCP server (W2), data
plane (W3). Each one has its own deny.
- The private MCP server is reached directly from Foundry, so the APIM kill switch and rate limit do not
- Governed data paths carry the user's own identity end to end (T1, T2, then T4 by OBO); the vendor
path ends at the gateway, and the legacy path (red) uses a shared key on purpose.
1. A persona signs in to Entra ID with MFA (the console uses device code on abw-test-client).
2. The user calls APIM /agents with an Entra token for Foundry (T1); APIM checks it and
3. APIM forwards to the Foundry Responses API; the user's token is passed on unchanged.
4. The agent calls a tool: Foundry sends the user's own OAuth token (T2, from a one-time
5. APIM checks audience, role, client and rate, then forwards to the MCP server (Wall 1).
6. The MCP server re-checks the token and swaps it for a data-plane token (OBO) using its
7. The MCP server calls Storage, Cosmos or Search as the user; the data plane's own roles
8. Every hop logs: APIM, MCP and Foundry telemetry flow to Log Analytics; MCP also writes
